source.title: Text-related functionality and dynamics of visual human pre-frontal activations revealed through neural network convergence
source.authors: A. Shoham; Rotem Broday-Dvir; Itay Yaron; G. Yovel; R. Malach

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Uses representational-structure comparisons between brain activity and neural networks as a tool to investigate brain function. It does not test whether independently trained models become more aligned with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The study compares brain-region RDMs with DNN RDMs, not alignment between independently trained models as they scale. Its DNN-to-brain correlations therefore do not test any listed version. It reports no numerical correlation values in the text for the main comparisons; those values are shown in figures.
record.test_reason: The study uses brain-to-DNN RSA (iEEG RDMs against VGG, CLIP-Image, CLIP-Text and GPT-2 RDMs) as a tool to infer prefrontal function. The authors frame this as brain–machine 'convergent evolution'. It never varies model scale or capability, seeds, mapping, or features, so no model-to-model version is tested. The between-DNN RDM correlations in Fig. 2B are descriptive only: four fixed models, 28 stimuli, and no capability axis.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that visually responsive fronto-parietal activity during visual memorization is uniquely predicted by text-based rather than visual DNNs. They add that this text-related association persists over time and shows an offset response, whereas the visual association declines rapidly.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RSA correlations between neural and DNN RDMs to investigate brain function; it does not compare independently trained model representations across scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported neural-to-DNN correlations vary by brain region, DNN type, time window, and image repetition.

fits_no_version.finding: In the 0.1–0.4 s window, only the text DNNs (CLIP-Text, GPT) have significant unique partial correlations with the fronto-parietal visual contacts. In face-selective ventral contacts, only VGG does. Fronto-parietal correlations stay at or below about 0.3 (noise ceiling 0.30), against roughly 0.6 for visual cortex.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Brain–DNN representational alignment differs by region: frontal visual responses align uniquely with text models, ventral visual cortex with vision models.

record.problems: The neural-to-DNN correlations do not directly establish representational convergence between models. The study uses 28 stimuli and 13 clinical patients; the authors note relatively noisy fronto-parietal responses and correlations below 0.3 even under optimal conditions. Main comparison values are presented in figures rather than stated numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional model-to-brain correlation rows extracted. The study also reports zero-order correlations, correlations across time windows, network layers, repetitions, shuffled-text controls, and human similarity ratings; these concern neural-to-model or human-to-brain associations rather than the listed model-to-model convergence versions.

untested.parts: Whether alignment between independently trained models rises with scale or capability; only four fixed models are used.
Whether vision–language alignment on paired data grows as models improve; CLIP-Image and CLIP-Text RDMs are compared only descriptively (Fig. 2B).
Whether models trained from different seeds share features; no seed comparison.
Mapping or stitching between models; not done.
Whether features or circuits recur across models; not examined.
How model-to-model convergence depends on measure or inputs; only cosine-distance RDMs on 28 stimuli are used, with no comparison of metrics.
Whether model-to-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared data or objectives; not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Rows R1–R8 are correctly linked to 'none' with state cannot_determine, because the values are figure-only. The inter-DNN RDM correlations in Fig. 2B are the only model-to-model measure in the paper. They are reported only in a figure and bear on no version as a test, so they are not recorded as missing. The brain–model 'convergence' in the title is a different construct from the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether representations of independently trained models become more aligned with scale and capability.
Whether vision and language model representations of paired images and captions align more as both models improve.
Whether different training seeds yield shared features or subspaces.
Whether representations can be mapped or stitched between models, or aligned through relative representations or without paired data.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Whether model-to-model convergence changes with similarity measures, settings, inputs, or distribution shifts.
Whether model-to-model alignment is incomplete or plateauing, or explained by shared data or objectives.

relation.reason: Its convergence framing concerns biological–artificial network parallels, rather than using any listed model-to-model claim version as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study uses brain–DNN representational similarities to investigate neural function. It neither tests nor relies on the catalog's finding of convergence among independently trained deep-learning models; using RSA alone does not establish T4.

source_check.notes: The publication year is 2025, rather than the pack's 2024. Figure-only coefficients are appropriately left unnumbered; these brain–DNN measurements cannot determine any listed claim version.
